title: Composed majority has a coarse threshold
statement: For every $0<\epsilon<1/4$, consider the sequence of composed majority functions whose dimension at index $k$ is $2+(2k+1)$. For each function, let its lower and upper threshold parameters be the unique biases in $(0,1)$ at which its probability of output $-1$ under independent biased signs is respectively $\epsilon$ and $1-\epsilon$; let its critical bias be the unique bias at which that probability is $1/2$. The sequence obtained by dividing the difference of the upper and lower threshold parameters by $4p(1-p)$ at the critical bias $p$ does not converge to $0$ as $k\to\infty$.
caveat: The conclusion is the negation of convergence of the normalized threshold width; the statement's auxiliary existence and uniqueness results are not included in this declaration.
